# Go Boil the Water

> Go Boil the Water: A Partner's Guide to Supporting Homebirth is a book by Noah Jenks for husbands and partners whose wives are planning a home birth. It is a presence guide, not a medical guide: it covers how a partner can show up well before labor, during the birth, and in the golden hour after. The paperback and Kindle editions are available on Amazon, and the audiobook is on Spotify.

The book draws on Noah's own experience (an adoption, two hospital births, and one home birth with his wife Katie) and on questionnaire responses from husbands, birth mothers, midwives, and doulas who have been through home births.

- [For Midwives and Doulas](https://goboilthewater.com/for-midwives-and-doulas/): resources for birth professionals to share with their clients' partners
- [Midwife and Doula Directory](https://goboilthewater.com/home-birth-midwife-directory/): coming soon, a free directory of home birth midwives and doulas

## Blog posts

- [What Does a Husband Do During a Home Birth?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/what-does-a-husband-do-during-a-home-birth/): The midwife runs the birth. Here's what your job actually is: staying close, staying steady, and doing the small useful things.
- [Is Home Birth Safe? What Partners Should Know](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/is-home-birth-safe/): What the biggest study found, where the medical groups disagree, and the three questions to ask your midwife.
- [My Wife Wants a Home Birth and I'm Not Sure. Now What?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/my-wife-wants-a-home-birth/): Your gut says no. What that fear is really about, and how to have the conversation without losing each other.
- [What's the Difference Between a Midwife and a Doula?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/midwife-vs-doula/): One is a medical provider and one is a support specialist. What each does at a home birth, and where you fit in.
- [What Happens If We Need to Transfer to the Hospital During a Home Birth?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/home-birth-hospital-transfer/): Most transfers aren't emergencies. What triggers one, how often it happens, and your job when the plan changes.
- [What Is the Golden Hour After Birth, and How Do I Protect It?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/golden-hour-after-birth/): The first stretch after birth matters more than most dads realize. At home, protecting it is your job.
- [How Do I Get Our House Ready for a Home Birth?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/prepare-house-for-home-birth/): A supply list, a test fill of the birth pool, and the conversation about what she wants the room to feel like.
- [Should I Go to the Prenatal Appointments?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/should-partner-go-to-prenatal-appointments/): Why partners who go to prenatal visits do better at the birth, and the questions worth asking the midwife.
- [How Do I Handle Family Who Think Home Birth Is Crazy?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/family-against-home-birth/): How partners can back their wife when family or friends push back on a home birth, with simple things to say.
- [How Do I Stay Calm When I Feel Helpless During Labor?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/feeling-helpless-during-labor/): Why partners feel helpless during labor, how their anxiety affects the room, and a simple 60-second reset.
- [What's It Like for a Husband to Catch His Own Baby at a Home Birth?](https://goboilthewater.com/blog/husband-catches-baby-home-birth/): Video interview with Rowan, a husband whose wife had two home births in Australia; he caught his daughter during a 30-minute water birth and shares advice for skeptical partners.
